title.narrative: Marie Stopes PSZ Scaling Up Access to Comprehensive SRHR in Zimbabwe 2022-24
Marie Stopes PSZ Scaling Up Access to Comprehensive SRHR in Zimbabwe 2022-25

description.narrative: Outcome 1: Underserved and marginalised women and girls in Zimbabwe access quality, voluntary Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) services Output 1.1. Quality comprehensive Sexual and Reproductive Health services delivered by MSI Reproductive Choices -Population Services Zimbabwe providers, reaching underserved and marginalised women and girls Output 1.2. Increased public sector capacity to deliver and sustain high-quality Sexual and Reproductive Health services Output 1.3. Increased private sector capacity to deliver and sustain high-quality Sexual and Reproductive Health services Outcome 2 - Underserved and marginalised women and girls in Zimbabwe are empowered with information and have community support to seek quality, voluntary Sexual and Reproductive Health services Output 2.1: Community mobilisers trained and equipped to deliver context specific gender and norm change interventions Output 2.2: Awareness-raising campaigns conducted that include signposting to quality assured service points Outcome 3: A more sustainable and supportive policy, clinical, and financial environment for the fulfilment of Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR) in Zimbabwe Output 3.1: Key local and national partnerships strengthened

Förslaget avser 40 MSEK, tre år efter program (april 2022 till mars 2025). Tjänsterna kommer att levereras genom 4 uppsökande team plus ett mobilt beredskapsteam, 3 statiska centra och 100 offentliga serviceplatser. MSI Reproductive Choices - Population Services Zimbabwe kommer att bevilja en ungdomsledd organisation (My Age Zimbabwe) och kommer att ha aktivitetsbaserat samarbete med andra ungdomsfokuserade organisationer för att säkerställa att räckvidden till ungdomar och ungdomar förbättras. MSI Reproductive Choices - Population Services Zimbabwe kommer att ha ett övergripande ansvar över sina partners, kapacitet, revision och kommer att ansvara för att leverera mål och rapportera till Sida.
Kvinnor, inklusive tonårsflickor, står inför många utmaningar när det gäller att få tillgång till tjänster för socialt och socialt skydds- och hälsoskyddstjänster som antingen inte kan vara tillgängliga eller tillgängliga men som inte är tillgängliga. För att ta itu med dessa utmaningar syftar bidraget till att skydda kvinnors och flickors hälsa och rättigheter i Zimbabwe och uppnå betydande minskningar av oönskade graviditeter, osäkra aborter och mödradödlighet. MSI Reproductive Choices-Populations Services Zimbabwe kommer att göra tjänsterna tillgängliga och tillgängliga genom att arbeta med samhällen och viktiga partners för att mobilisera och sensibilisera både kvinnor och män.

The proposal is for a MSEK40, three year follow on programme (April 2022 to March 2025). The services will be delivered through 4 outreach teams plus a mobile emergency response team, 3 static centres and 100 public sector service sites. MSI Reproductive Choices - Population Services Zimbabwe will sub-grant a youth led organisation (My Age Zimbabwe) and will have activity based partnering with other youth focused organization to ensure reach to adolescents and young people is improved. MSI Reproductive Choices - Population Services Zimbabwe will have an overall responsibility over its partners, capacity, auditing and will be responsible for delivery of objectives and reporting to Sida.
Women including adolescent girls face a lot of challenges in accessing SRH service which could either be not available or available but not accessible due to economic or social reasons. To address these challenges the contribution aims to protect the health and rights of women and girls in Zimbabwe and achieve significant reductions in unwanted pregnancies, unsafe abortions and maternal mortality. MSI Reproductive Choices-Populations Services Zimbabwe will make the services available and accessible by working with the communities and key partners to mobilise and sensitise both women and men.

Final results
Outreach services were offered in 18 districts, making sexual and reproductive services more accessible to marginalized communities. Throughout the project, a total of 860,051 clients were engaged, reaching 125% of the intended client target. Clients between the ages of 20 and 24 represented 27% (234,421), whereas those aged 15 to 19 made up 12%. The project averted an estimated 301,000 unintended pregnancies, approximately 860 maternal deaths and 78,000 unsafe abortions. Thirteen percent of clients were identified as poor, while 4% were categorized as severely poor according to the Multi-poverty Indices. It was also observed that 7% of the clients had disabilities
The project achieved an estimated total of USD 22.7 million (USD 7.3 million in Year 1; USD 7.8 million in Year 2; and USD 7.6 million in Year 3) in direct health care cost savings.
The percentage of adolescent clients served rose by 3% compared to the project's initial phase. The accomplishment was credited to the sub granting of My Age, a youth organization committed to executing adolescent-friendly demand creation and awareness programs. The call centre functioned as a valuable support channel for helping adolescent girls and young women obtain information on family planning, sexual and reproductive health, and reproductive rights, as well as connections to services. The call center managed 55,574 incoming calls throughout the project's duration. Out of the life of project service provision reach, 27% of the clients (14,999) were directed from the call centre. Six percent of these clients were teenagers, 7% were individuals adopting family planning, and 1% were new users. A total of 1,352 referrals were issued from the call centre to alternative service providers for services not offered by MSI\PSZ.
To enhance community understanding and acceptance of contraception and safe abortion, the project organized Values Clarification and Attitude Transformation workshops for parliamentarians, religious figures, and traditional leaders. The HE CAN SGBV campaigns confronted detrimental religious and cultural traditions that sustain SGBV and motivated communities to unite as a collective voice against these customs.
The project assisted 100 public health facilities through training, coaching, and mentoring of nursing staff in clinical governance and quality, which encompassed infection prevention control, management of medical emergencies, quality assurance, inventory management, and data integrity. This contributes to make the health facilities more sustainable by enhancing provider capacity in key clinical areas.
The Young Peoples Digital Interventions Toolkit, created and released in 2024, offers a wide array of digital solutions, such as accessible mobile apps, online platforms, and creative assistive technologies, specifically designed to meet the varied SRHR requirements of adolescents and young individuals. More than 2,000 young individuals have downloaded the Toolkit at the time of reporting.
Advocacy efforts by MSI\PSZ and the Safe Abortion Coalition played a role in the adoption of the updated Comprehensive Abortion Care Guidelines. The coalition gathered stakeholders focused on safe abortion and supported the government in adapting the guidelines.
MSI\PSZ held discussions on domestic health financing, contributing to the increase in domestic health funding from 10.6% in 2022 to 11.2% in 2023.
YEAR TWO RESULTS 322,951 clients were reached across all service delivery channels in 2023. 12% of the clients reached were young people under the age of 19 and 28% were between 20-24 years. The contribution is making inroads to reach young people with SRHR services leveraging on the partnership with My Age a youth organisation. My Age is conducted a "Know Your Service" campaign that specifically targeted young people with information of available services and linking them to the service of their choice. Post Abortion Care services were provided to almost 10 000 adolescent girls and young women. 44,242 long-Acting Reversible Contraceptives were administered which was a 48% increase from the 1st year of implementation. 574,628 short-term Family Planning methods consisting of injectables, and oral contraceptives commodities were issued. 115 permanent Family Planning procedures were performed.
In collaboration with the MoHCC, the Emergency Medical Response outreach team responded to emergencies including the cholera and typhoid out breaks. The response focused on general clinical support and integrating Sexual Reproductive Health and Family Planning into the emergency response.
To strengthen the service delivery with public institutions, the contribution supported the training in Long-Acting Reversible Contraceptives (LARCs), clinical quality and data quality assurance; provision of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and general technical support. The public sector channel contributed 91% share of the 322,951 total number of clients reached by the project in 2023.
The contribution played a key role in ensuring an inclusive and comprehensive review of the Comprehensive Abortion Care (CAC) guidelines through supporting participation of private and public obstetrician-gynaecologists in the process. the National Comprehensive Abortion Care (CA) Guidelines have now been signed. The guidelines now focus on comprehensive abortion care and not only post-abortion care. The CAC guidelines also highlight that unsafe abortion is one of the major public health problems in Zimbabwe. This recognition opens up space for more work to be done in this area.
YEAR ONE RESULTS
MSI (Population Services Zimbabwe) is implementing a three-year SRHR programme to increase the use of quality comprehensive contraception and post-abortion care (PAC) services among underserved population. The programme which is a second phase of a previous programme has completed its first year of implementation.
The report was submitted in time together with the financial reports as per the agreement. The report documents the progress in implementing the Scaling up Access to Comprehensive Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights for Women and Girls in Zimbabwe program during April - December 2022 activity period, summarising the key achievements and the key program outputs.
About 207,955 client visits were recorded across all channels, against a target of 115,027.
About 2300 Post Abortion Care services were provided to clients through the Static Centres. The project reached 22,181 adolescents aged between 15 to 19 years during this reporting period. Through community-based mobilisers (CBMs), radio programmes, social media and the MSI-PSZ Contact Centre, MSI-PSZ estimates that it reached over 4 million people with accurate rights-based SRHR information in 2022.
The sub grant partnership with MyAge resulted in a 2% increase in the reach to adolescents. The youth-led Organisation set up a studio in Masvingo that enables the recording of digital conversations and acts as a youth hub. The studio still needs some work to bring out its full potential.
There was a significant reach of people with disabilities who accounted for about 10% of the total reach.
Work to counter opposition of SRHR continues and MSI-PSZ supported the development of the Family Planning strategy through both financial and technical support to Zimbabwe National Family Planning Council. MSI-PSZ also worked in collaboration with WHO and the Ministry of Health to draft the review of the 2014 Comprehensive Abortion Care guidelines. Although MSI in Zimbabwe has been doing advocacy work on safe abortion and overall policy environment the assessment is that the capacity in advocacy and policy work as well as capacity to monitor and follow up the same needs further strengthening following staff turn over a couple of years. Dialogues with the partner will continue to try and resolve these capacity gaps.
The report notes the unprecedented increase on rentals and utility bills in Zimbabwe during the implementation year, resulting in over expenditure on the other direct costs budget line.
The challenge regarding staff retention in both PSZ Static Centres and the public sector persisted during the year, which limited the numbers of providers who are trained on Long-Acting Reversible Contraception provision as well as other SRHR services such as STI screening and treatment.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
